habitat: Thickets in dry mixed bushveld, riverine forest, and the foot of rocky bush-covered hills and termite mounds. Also gardens in some regions.
summary: A common endemic resident. Distinguished by a white breast and a white wing-bar. The immature is well spotted. The morning call is a repeated swee-swer, and it also has a song with mimicry. The Kemp name Whitethroated Robin and the code RB were left unchanged.

viewNotes.note: White breast and a white wing-bar.

calls.description: Repeated 'swee-swer' in the early morning, and a quiet 'tseep'. It also has a song with mimicry. The grade A call is from Kruger near Skukuza. The filename does not name the species.

research.note: Newman calls it a common endemic resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The grade A call is from Kruger and the filename does not name the species. The Kemp name Whitethroated Robin and the code RB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^13=8192 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 4096–16384.
